exhibits.title: The World Wide Web
exhibits.change: Linked pages anyone could publish and anyone could read.
exhibits.context: Tim Berners-Lee proposed a hypertext system at CERN, created HTML, HTTP and URLs, and released the web royalty-free in 1993.
exhibits.significance: Turned the internet into a universal medium for publishing and knowledge.

exhibits.title: The Hubble Space Telescope
exhibits.change: A telescope above the atmosphere.
exhibits.context: After a flawed mirror was corrected by a 1993 servicing mission, Hubble measured the universe's expansion rate, observed distant galaxies and helped reveal the accelerating expansion (1998).
exhibits.significance: Some of the most important — and most widely seen — scientific images ever made.

exhibits.title: The Graphical Web Browser
exhibits.change: Images and text together on one page, with a click.
exhibits.context: NCSA Mosaic made the web visual and easy; web use exploded within two years.
exhibits.significance: The window through which most people first met the internet.

exhibits.title: Real-Time 3D Worlds
exhibits.change: Interactive worlds rendered in three dimensions, instantly.
exhibits.context: Games and reusable game engines of the mid-1990s, together with consumer 3D graphics cards, made real-time 3D common; shared online worlds followed.
exhibits.significance: Graphics processors built for games later powered scientific computing and AI.

exhibits.title: Robots on Mars
exhibits.change: Wheeled explorers drove across another planet.
exhibits.context: Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity and Perseverance found evidence of ancient water; the Ingenuity helicopter flew in Mars's thin air in 2021.
exhibits.significance: Remote exploration of other worlds.

exhibits.title: The International Space Station

when.display: first module 1998; continuously inhabited since November 2000

regions.note: US, Russia, Europe, Japan and Canada.

exhibits.change: People have lived in orbit without a break for over two decades.
exhibits.context: Assembled in orbit from modules launched by several nations, the ISS hosts research on biology, physics and long-duration spaceflight.
exhibits.significance: Sustained human presence beyond Earth, built by rivals working together.

exhibits.title: Wikipedia
exhibits.change: An encyclopaedia written, checked and corrected by volunteers, free to all.
exhibits.context: Now in over 300 languages, it relies on sourcing rules and open editing histories — a large-scale experiment in collaborative knowledge.
exhibits.significance: Collective knowledge at planetary scale.

exhibits.title: The Human Genome

regions.note: An international public consortium and a private effort.

exhibits.change: The three billion letters of human DNA were read.
exhibits.context: The Human Genome Project cost about three billion dollars over thirteen years; sequencing a genome now costs a tiny fraction of that. The same methods reveal the Neanderthal and Denisovan ancestry shown in the earliest galleries.
exhibits.significance: Genetic medicine, ancestry research and the reading of the deep human past.

exhibits.title: The Smartphone
exhibits.change: A networked computer, camera, map and library in a pocket.
exhibits.context: Earlier devices (IBM Simon, BlackBerry, Japanese i-mode phones) combined phones with data; the iPhone (2007) and Android (2008) made the touchscreen smartphone the dominant form. Within fifteen years most adults on Earth owned one.
exhibits.significance: The first technology in history used by most of humanity at once.

uncertainty.note: Smartphones had many predecessors; 2007 marks the design that became dominant.

exhibits.title: Cheap Solar Power
exhibits.change: Solar panel prices fell by around ninety percent in a decade.
exhibits.context: Manufacturing scale and learning drove the cost of photovoltaic modules down steeply, making solar one of the cheapest sources of new electricity in many regions.
exhibits.significance: A central tool in the shift away from fossil fuels.

sources.note: Our World in Data page is general background only.

exhibits.title: Deep Learning
exhibits.change: Neural networks trained on vast data learned to see, translate, speak and write.
exhibits.context: In 2012 a deep convolutional network (AlexNet) won the ImageNet challenge by a large margin, using graphics processors. The transformer architecture (2017) led to large language models in the 2020s. Their capabilities, limits and risks are actively debated.
exhibits.significance: Computing began to do tasks once thought to require human judgement.

uncertainty.note: Long-term impacts are unknown and contested.

exhibits.title: Genome Editing
exhibits.change: A bacterial defence system repurposed to edit DNA precisely.
exhibits.context: CRISPR–Cas9 made editing genes fast and cheap. The first CRISPR-based therapy, for sickle-cell disease, was approved in 2023. Ethical debate intensified after an unauthorised editing of human embryos in 2018.
exhibits.significance: The ability to rewrite genetic code — with enormous promise and hard questions.

exhibits.title: The Higgs Boson

regions.note: Thousands of physicists from many countries.

exhibits.change: The last predicted particle of the Standard Model was found.
exhibits.context: The ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider detected the particle predicted in 1964 by Higgs, Englert, Brout and others.
exhibits.significance: Confirmed how fundamental particles acquire mass.

exhibits.title: A Global Climate Agreement
exhibits.change: Nearly every nation agreed to limit global warming.
exhibits.context: Under the Paris Agreement, countries set their own emissions targets to keep warming well below 2 °C. Whether commitments are sufficient and met is the subject of ongoing scientific and political debate.
exhibits.significance: Recognition that the industrial energy system reshaping the planet must change.

exhibits.title: Reusable Rockets
exhibits.change: A rocket's first stage flew back and landed upright.
exhibits.context: SpaceX's Falcon 9 booster landed in December 2015; reuse has since lowered the cost of reaching orbit and increased launch rates.
exhibits.significance: Cheaper access to space for satellites and science.

exhibits.title: Gravitational Waves
exhibits.change: Ripples in spacetime from two black holes merging a billion light-years away.
exhibits.context: Laser interferometers measured a change in length far smaller than a proton, confirming a century-old prediction of general relativity.
exhibits.significance: A new way to observe the universe.

exhibits.title: Half of Humanity Online
exhibits.change: For the first time, most people on Earth used the internet.
exhibits.context: International Telecommunication Union estimates passed the halfway mark around 2019, largely via mobile phones. Access remains very unequal between and within countries.
exhibits.significance: A species-wide network — still unfinished.

exhibits.title: New Lunar Landings

when.display: 2019 (first soft landing on the far side); 2023 (near the south pole)

exhibits.change: New nations reached places on the Moon no one had landed before.
exhibits.context: China's Chang'e 4 landed on the far side of the Moon, relaying signals through a satellite; India's Chandrayaan-3 landed near the lunar south pole.
exhibits.significance: Space exploration became multipolar.

exhibits.title: mRNA Vaccines
exhibits.change: Vaccines designed from a genetic sequence within days.
exhibits.context: Decades of research — including Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman's work on modified nucleosides — allowed COVID-19 mRNA vaccines to be developed and tested within a year of the virus being sequenced.
exhibits.significance: A flexible platform for rapid vaccine development.

exhibits.title: Predicting Protein Shapes
exhibits.change: AI predicted the 3D structure of proteins from their sequence.
exhibits.context: AlphaFold 2 achieved near-experimental accuracy in the CASP14 assessment (2020); predicted structures for hundreds of millions of proteins were released publicly.
exhibits.significance: A long-standing problem in biology largely solved with machine learning.

exhibits.title: The James Webb Space Telescope
exhibits.change: An infrared eye, a million and a half kilometres away, seeing the first galaxies.
exhibits.context: Webb's 6.5-metre segmented mirror unfolded in space. It observes galaxies from the first few hundred million years after the Big Bang and analyses the atmospheres of exoplanets.
exhibits.significance: Humanity's furthest look back in time so far.
